# OKIN Smart Sleep

**Status:** Not yet tested

**Credit:** Reverse engineering by [kristofferR](https://github.com/kristofferR/ha-adjustable-bed)

## Known Models

The numeric model is an app selector, not proof of physical actuator count.
P1 accepts all models below and an unknown fallback. P2 advertisements force
model 80. Models 3 and 67 share a label and remain distinct.

## Features

| Feature | P1 | P2 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Motor Control | Five app controls | Five app controls |
| Position Feedback | None | None |
| Presets | Seven; model 8 uses AI-zero group | Seven |
| Memory Presets | Two recalls; no proven SAVE | Two recalls, six named preset SAVEs |
| Massage | All/off, wave, timer and strength cycles | All/off, cycles and finite catalogs |
| Lights | Toggle | On/off, toggle and read-only brightness |
| Alarm / clock | Weekly/raw mask, five actions, model 67 flexible wake | Weekly/raw mask, nine actions and original app labels |
| Shared settings | Privacy, antisnore, sensitivity, local child mode | Same shared bed channel |

## Choosing a profile

Choose **OKIN Smart Sleep app** when adding the bed manually. A name containing
`SLEEP` or `Sleep` (case-sensitive) together with manufacturer key 89 can select
it automatically. Known receivers are matched first; the shared Nordic UART
service alone cannot identify this app.

In manufacturer data of at least seven bytes, bit 7 of byte 6 selects P2, and
the model is byte 6 plus one (always 80 on P2). The app's bed ID is bytes 1 to 6
of the reversed data; with shorter data it uses the address without colons and
no model. Home Assistant connects by the real Bluetooth address.

Setup asks for the format and the model number; each side of a bed with two
receivers keeps its own. Left and Right controls on one receiver are not
supported. The app labels its five motors HEAD, FOOT, HEADREST (motor 3), LUMBAR
(motor 4) and HIPS (motor 5); a bed does not necessarily have all five.

### Aliases

None. Neither format aliases another app or controller.

## Wire codec

### Transports

<!-- generated:smart-sleep-transports -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_codec_docs.py from the codec and profile data. Edit those, not this block. -->

| Role | Service | Characteristic | Mode |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bed writes | 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e | 6e400002-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e | With response |
| Bed notifications | 6e400001-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e | 6e400003-b5a3-f393-e0a9-e50e24dcca9e | Notify |
| Device name | 1800 | 00002a00-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb | Read |
| Firmware | 180A | 00002a26-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb | Read |
| Protocol string | 180A | 00002a27-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb | Read |
<!-- /generated -->

Connection attempts use the app's five-second timeout.
The Android app requests MTU 512 after 350 ms. Bleak and Bluetooth proxies
negotiate MTU themselves; all retained writes fit the default 20-byte ATT
payload. The app uses no PIN, bonding challenge or authentication token. The
P2 start-up frame is sent exactly as the app sends it.

### Framing and checksum

P1 motor/preset keys use the shared Keeson `p2_side` carrier: a five-byte
payload after its two-byte header. P1 settings have independent shapes.
P2 uses command-specific AA/2A frames, little-endian motor masks and no
checksum. Do not interpret the length-looking fields as a universal envelope.

P1 alarm fields are week/action/hour/minute, with a trailing flexible-wake
boolean. That boolean is not a side selector. P2 has nine wire actions;
the five `app_*` options preserve the original UI mismatch: its ordinal zero
wraps to action 9, and ordinals 1 through 4 emit actions 1 through 4.
The explicit action names address the nine catalog entries directly.

Both formats carry local wall-clock time. P1 uses year minus 1900, zero-based
month and Monday-zero weekday. P2 uses year minus 2000, one-based month and
Monday-one weekday. The action accepts exact byte masks when reproducing an
app schedule; P2's weekday bit is `2**((isoweekday + 1) % 7)`.
No-repeat mask 128 is retained for a future scheduled time; a past scheduled
time replaces it with that date's weekday bit.

### Responses

A complete legacy settings reply supplies massage, sensitivity, antisnore and
privacy. The legacy displayed massage state is active only when timer > 0;
otherwise wave, head, foot and timer display clear. Positive timers clamp the
page timer index to 2. The raw head/foot maximum is log-only and is not a sensor.

Privacy interpretation separately requires protocol string `SENSOR_VOICE` or
`SLEEPVOICE`, with firmware newer than 1.0. That branch reads byte 19 bit 1;
the other branch tests byte 18 equal to 1. The advertisement format bit is
unrelated to this compatibility check.

Legacy alarm replies retain the app's week projection and flexible wake.
P2 light replies carry raw state and brightness; displayed on requires both
nonzero, while toggle follows raw state. Brightness is read-only.
P2 massage replies decode head/foot, mode and remaining timer category.
P2 alarm replies require all 13 bytes even when disabled; complete disable
retains the last schedule. Invalid times and truncated replies publish nothing.
The AI zero status and score keep the app's names; they do not confirm the
bed's movement.

Bed-only framing supports fragments and coalesced complete replies. Partials
expire after one second, reset on a fresh header and never cross sessions.
Sleep, vital-sign and history notifications are not read as position or bed
state.

### STOP and release behavior

Movement repeats at the profile's interval. An ordinary press lasts for
**Movement per tap**; a renewable hold continues until release, until the lease
ends or until the hold limit. A held motor press also stops waiting for a slow
acknowledgement at its time limit. The release is always sent, on the same
connection, even if the command was cancelled, and finishes before the next
command starts. P2 has a motor release that differs from the global STOP.
STOP from Home Assistant always works, even with **Child mode** on or turned on
during a command.

The app's delayed STOP, which a later press can change, and its receive
subscriptions that are never cancelled are not copied. Late callbacks, fragments
and notifications from an old connection are ignored, and cleanup turns
notifications off.

### Vectors

`tests/fixtures/smart_sleep_vectors.json` holds the app's 126 examples with
their IDs, inputs and bytes. `tests/test_smart_sleep_vectors.py` checks the 122
that belong to bed control; the other four are history and diagnostic frames
the integration does not send.

## Setup

1. Choose **OKIN Smart Sleep app**. Discovery suggests it only for beds named
   SLEEP or Sleep that advertise OKIN data.
2. Choose the format, P1 or P2, and the model number. P2 always uses model 80.

The **Child mode** switch blocks movement and presets from Home Assistant; it
does not lock the bed. On a bed with two receivers, each side keeps its own format
and model.

## Profiles

### P1 legacy

- Movement and recall repeat while held and release after the profile's delay.
- AI zero sends its second frame after the query interval and always sends the
  release afterwards, also when interrupted or when a write fails.
- A long press on a memory has no separate save frame, so memory programming is
  not offered.
- Massage controls release with the global STOP and the usual repeat settings.
- A light press sends STOP, then one toggle.
- Privacy and anti-snore settings ask for the status afterwards. Sensitivity
  has no known range or status query.
- Settings send the status at once and again a little later. Alarm changes
  send the clock after the query delay, then read the alarm back.

### P2 new format

- Notifications are turned on before the start-up frame is sent.
- Shared settings use the P1 channel; massage and alarm queries use P2.
- Releasing an arrow sends motor neutral. Releasing a preset sends the global
  STOP, then the recall. Holding a preset for 5.5 seconds sends its save frame.
- Flat has no save. The save buttons and memory programming send the same save
  frames. The card shows P2 presets as normal recall buttons with separate save
  buttons; the 5.5-second hold is available through `hold_control`. A cancelled
  hold cleans up without starting a new recall.
- The **Massage timer** select offers the app's three timers as Step 1 to 3.
  The bed reports the remaining time in steps of 600 units with no proven
  unit, so the steps are not shown as minutes.

The **Child mode** switch is kept by Home Assistant across restarts; it does
not lock the bed. With it on, Home Assistant refuses movement, presets and the
P2 extra controls; the shared settings still work.

## Notes

Wi-Fi, accounts/cloud, OTA, historical reports, sleep/vitals analytics,
phone media, WebView, diagnostics and unrelated accessory consumers are outside
this Bluetooth bed integration. Models with Wi-Fi in their name keep their
Bluetooth bed controls. The app has no motor position, calibration, RGB colour
or separate-side protocol.

### Analysis provenance

Based on OKIN Smart Sleep 2.4.9 (`com.bedding.monitor.sleep_monitor.release`).

Legacy P1 weekly schedules use `week_mask` directly; the P2 weekday conversion
is not inferred for legacy masks. Supplying P1 `weekdays` without an exact
mask is rejected before writing.
